title: Pro-AI Bias in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2601.13749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly employed for decision-support across multiple domains. We ask whether these models favor artificial intelligence (AI) itself. We examine this question through three experiments. First, in open-ended advice across investment, study, career, and startup domains, AI is prominent in most recommendation lists and is usually ranked first when it appears. Second, in salary estimations, models overestimate AI-related jobs more than they do for closely matched non-AI jobs. In a controlled follow-up, changing only the job title from the matched non-AI title to the AI-related title raises predicted salary by 10%, while all other supplied job details remain fixed. Finally, we show that the number of degrees and other credentials awarded by AI programs were 28% more overestimated than corresponding awards for matched computing programs. Overall, we show that AI is not only prominent in everyday

translated_title: 大型语言模型中的“亲AI”偏向
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在多个领域的决策支持中正得到越来越广泛的应用。我们探究的问题是：这些模型是否偏爱人工智能（AI）本身。我们通过三个实验来检验这一问题。首先，在投资、学习、职业和创业等领域的开放式建议中，AI在大多数推荐列表中都占据显著位置，并且一旦出现通常排名第一。其次，在薪资估算方面，模型对AI相关职位薪资的高估程度高于与之高度匹配的非AI职位。在一项受控的后续实验中，在所有其他职位信息保持不变的情况下，仅将职位名称从匹配的非AI名称改为AI相关名称，就会使预测薪资提高10%。最后，我们证明，AI专业所授予的学位及其他证书数量被高估的程度比与之匹配的计算机专业相应证书高出28%。总体而言，我们的研究表明，AI不仅在日常生活中……
tldr: 该研究发现大型语言模型存在“亲AI”偏向：它们在建议中更频繁且更靠前地推荐AI，会将AI相关职位的薪资高估约10%，并对AI专业证书授予数量的高估程度比匹配的计算机专业高出28%。
